abstract: Co-transcriptional binding (imprinting) of mRNAs by the Rpb4 subunit of RNA polymerase II (RNA pol II) coordinates transcription with cytoplasmic mRNA fates. However, the genomic features of Rpb4-target genes and their cross-talk with decay factors remain unclear. In this study, in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, we demonstrate that genes producing Rpb4-imprinted mRNAs exhibit higher TR paired with lower levels of RNA pol II backtracking. Notably, these loci act as specific genomic targets for the 5'-3' exoribonuclease Xrn1, that has also been shown to act as transcriptional activator in a set of yeast genes, displaying prominent Xrn1 enrichment along their gene bodies. In accordance, XRN1 deletion alters global RNA pol II occupancy, leads to a decrease in TR and reduces growth severely in a rpb4{Delta} background. Furthermore, we show that Rpb4 physically interacts with Xrn1 in a strictly RNA-dependent -imprinting manner. Together, our findings uncover a functional Rpb4 Xrn1 axis that connects efficient transcription elongation with mRNA imprinting and turnover.
